subject.title: [Bug]: Teams app removal/re-add retains prior DM session history

question: For true Microsoft Teams app-management removal, should OpenClaw isolate future messages by rotating/staling the route-matched session and removing the cached Teams conversation reference while preserving transcript files?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the behavior controls retained personal-chat context and proactive conversation reachability after app removal, so automation should not choose the privacy-retention boundary alone.

options.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
options.body: Treat bot-visible Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcripts unless a separate retention policy changes that.

options.title: Require destructive retention behavior
options.body: Pause the linked PR until app removal deletes or archives retained Teams DM transcript/session data under an explicit data-retention policy.

options.title: Document as platform-limited only
options.body: Decline server-side session resets for Teams removal flows and document that only explicit user reset commands can clear OpenClaw context.

recommendation.title: Use non-destructive reset plus reference removal
recommendation.body: Treat bot-visible Teams app removal as a session boundary, clear the proactive conversation reference, and preserve transcripts unless a separate retention policy changes that.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent Teams conversation-store and retained-state history for deciding the security-sensitive retention boundary.
